newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan gov't calls for calm ahead of march.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan gov't calls for calm ahead of march.

text.p: Venezuela's Interior Minister Jose Guillermo Andueza called for calm Thursday ahead of a large march in Caracas against President Rafael Caldera's government.

In a statement broadcast on local radio Andueza said people should "remain calm in the face of a wave of rumors...caused by sectors which want to create a climate of alarm and concern which does not exist at all."
Andueza did not say what the rumors were.

The interior minister made the statement after announcing that public sector employees working in central Caracas had been given the afternoon off to reduce congestion in the center at the end of a march led by striking university professors.

Security has been stepped up in the capital due to the march, which was also to be attended by workers of bankrupt airline Viasa, striking blood bank workers, students and other union and political representatives.
Local and international financial markets have been awash with rumors in recent weeks, including reports of Caldera's deteriorating health and planned coup attempts.
Government officials have said the rumors were unfounded.
